key_insight: ProAS fixes uniform trajectory-level credit assignment in critic-free LLM-agent RL by shaping advantages with a progress-aware reference graph so early, pivotal actions and invalid actions are treated differently.
engineering_relevance: It offers a plug-and-play way to improve multi-turn agent training without adding critic overhead, making group-based RL more practical for scalable agentic systems.
method: Build a dynamic Agentic Reference Graph (ARG) to track progress-aware structure across trajectories.
Apply Masking Unreasonable Incentives (MUI) to suppress rewards for structurally invalid actions in preferred paths.
Use Asymmetric Penalty Redistribution (APR) to spread blame more accurately for early mistakes in unpreferred trajectories.
evidence_signal: Across Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, ProAS improved group-based baselines to new SOTA, reaching 91.9%/94.3% success on ALFWorld and 66.7%/70.8% on WebShop, while speeding convergence by up to 2.44×.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality of the ARG, so imperfect or distilled graphs may reduce credit-assignment accuracy and should be validated carefully.
paper_title: ProAS: A Progress-Aware Advantage Shaping Framework for Multi-Turn Agentic Reinforcement Learning
